purpose: Test three user-proposed branches without promoting them to fact: (A) a common mold/mandrel behind Egyptian gold phallic objects, (B) deliberate masculinization of female rulers/deities, and (C) whether iconographic absence of a laryngeal prominence can reveal concealed biological sex.
claim_ceiling: Hypotheses only. No source currently establishes that Osiris or Seth were biologically female, that a phallic mold was taken from Osiris, that a false phallus detached during ritual, or that a state conspiracy concealed deity sex.

known_controls: Mendes 1902 Nesbanebdjedet gold phallus sheath, primary-source documented
Egyptian Museum Cairo JE 56935 gold sheet penis amulet
Egyptian Museum Cairo JE 56967 gold foil phallus amulet
published Qurna gilded resin penis-and-scrotum model
A_SHARED_MANDREL.decision_rule: Matching overall size alone is insufficient. Shared tooling requires homologous construction marks or repeatable three-dimensional geometry. Even a shared mandrel reconstructs a workshop standard, not Osiris anatomy, unless an independent inscription/provenance explicitly binds the template to an Osirian relic.

positive_precedent: Hatshepsut was a female pharaoh represented in many monumental statues as the ideal male king with false beard and male royal regalia.
Met notes that Hatshepsut's inscriptions still preserve feminine grammatical forms/personal name; the masculine image was royal ideology, not a demonstrated attempt to hide her sex.
The late Amarna succession includes a female pharaoh Neferneferuaten; candidate identity remains debated between Nefertiti and Meritaten in current scholarship.
counterevidence_to_total_masculinity_con: Egyptian religion openly preserved powerful female deities including Sekhmet, a goddess of war, violence and protection.
UCL's creation synthesis explicitly calls Osiris and Seth gods/sons, Isis and Nephthys goddesses, with Osiris the elder son and Seth his brother.
Book of the Dead 42 explicitly maps the phallus to Osiris and the back to Seth.
B_FEMALE_RULER_OR_DEITY_MASCULINIZATION.conclusion: Royal visual language could masculinize a known woman, so gender presentation and biological sex must be separated. The checked corpus does not support a hidden-female Osiris/Seth hypothesis.

reason: The laryngeal prominence is sexually dimorphic on average but overlaps between individuals; it is more prominent in males, not exclusive to males.
Egyptian royal and divine art is strongly idealized and omits/reshapes anatomical details according to convention.
Therefore presence/absence of a carved or drawn laryngeal prominence cannot establish biological sex.
C_ADAMS_APPLE_ICONOGRAPHY.acceptable_for_mummies: If preserved, laryngeal CT morphology can be recorded as a secondary feature, but pelvic morphology, skull, soft-tissue genital anatomy when preserved, and ancient DNA/sex-chromosome evidence have much higher evidentiary value.

checked_examples.result: Female ruler who deliberately used male kingly iconography; not a male pharaoh later discovered to be female.
Female pharaoh attested in museum cataloguing; exact identity debated. This is a succession/identity problem, not a mummy sex reversal.
CT reconstruction did not show feminine pelvic traits; genetic/pedigree work treats KV55 as male and probable father of Tutankhamun.
Male; JAMA report notes a well-developed penis, despite stylized/feminized Amarna royal art.
Genetic study reports Y-chromosome lineage in Ramesses III and Unknown Man E.
Unidentified female mummy later identified as Queen Tiye; not a king mis-sexed as male.

D_MALE_RULERS_FOUND_FEMALE_AUDIT.important_control: Non-royal Egyptian mummies can be mis-sexed from iconography or incomplete morphology and later corrected by CT/DNA. Therefore the audit should remain open, but no checked royal case currently supplies the proposed pattern.

propaganda_test.hypothesis: Masculine royal/divine imagery was used because male audiences would not mobilize for goddesses.
counterexamples: Sekhmet was explicitly a female war deity and symbol of destructive/protective power.
Hatshepsut openly ruled as a female king while adopting masculine regalia.
Egyptian ritual texts can identify a male king with female deities such as Sekhmet/Bast in ideological language.
propaganda_test.better_model: Egyptian kingship had strongly masculine conventional imagery, but divine/royal gender could be symbolically fluid at the level of roles and identifications. This does not by itself imply hidden biological sex.

new_gates.goal: Acquire calibrated measurements and manufacturing signatures for the Mendes sheath, JE 56935, JE 56967, Met 23.10.23 and other comparable gold phallic objects.
Build a ruler-by-ruler table using CT, pelvis/skull morphology, preserved genital anatomy and DNA where available; record prior identification vs measured biological sex.
Run the same Mendes/Osiris/Banebdjedet provenance filters over vulva/cowrie/pubis/female-genital covers and fertility objects to detect search bias or mirrored ritual technology.
Catalog Osiris figures with separately made genitalia, insertion sockets, repairs, missing genital components or detachable parts and compare attachment geometry.
